findings.title: `_window` couples the period predicate to a truthy `extra` dict
findings.description: `_window` takes a generic `extra: dict[str, Any] | None`. It merges that dict into the bind parameters, and then, if `extra` is truthy, it appends a hard-coded `period = %(period)s` clause. Nothing in the signature says that `extra` must contain a `period` key. A future caller who passes any other extra parameter would get a `period` predicate with no bound value. That fails at execution time with a psycopg missing-parameter error. A caller who passes an empty dict would silently drop the period filter. Make `period: int | None` an explicit keyword argument and add the clause when it is not `None`. That removes the implicit contract and the untyped dict.

findings.title: Duplicated ceiling check between the executor closure and `_admit_rows`
findings.description: The `if count > max_rows` branch inside `_read` and the later `_admit_rows(read.count, max_rows)` both encode the same ceiling comparison, in `get_candlesticks` and again in `get_trades`. The two checks have to stay in step: if the first is relaxed, `_admit_rows` still refuses, and if the second is removed, the response is built from empty rows and reports a false `count`. The two near-identical `_read` closures also repeat the seek, 404, count, guard and fetch sequence. Consider a shared helper that takes the counter and fetcher and returns `_Read`, with a single predicate such as `read.over_ceiling`.

findings.title: Load test relies on a private pool attribute and class-level mutable state
findings.description: `_client` reaches into `pool._pool` with `# noqa: SLF001`. This is a psycopg_pool private detail, and a library upgrade can break it silently. The coverage is also incomplete: connections created after startup (pool growth or replacement) never receive the recording cursor factory. For assertion 2 the effect is that a missed connection records nothing. The `not fetches` assertion then passes vacuously, because the guard on `counts` only proves that some connection was recorded. `_RecordingCursor.statements` is also a class-level list that tests reassign, which makes the recorder shared global state. Pass `kwargs={"cursor_factory": ...}` when constructing the pool, or patch a connection class. Alternatively, assert on server-side statement logging.

findings.title: `TradeRecord.from_row` depends on positional indexing of `TradeRow.values`
findings.description: `TradeRow.values` is `tuple[Any, ...]`, and `from_row` reads `values[0]` to `values[7]` by position. The order is implied by `TRADE_VALUE_COLUMNS`, which is derived from `TRADE_COLUMNS` minus `market_ticker`. This contradicts the module's claim that a column added to the repository mapping is served without an edit. Reordering or adding a trade column would shift the fields without a type error. This is weaker than the candle path, which walks `CANDLE_COLUMNS`. Build the record from `zip(TRADE_VALUE_COLUMNS, values)`, or have the reader return named fields. `TradeRow.values` is also typed `Any`, which hides mismatches at the boundary.

findings.title: `tape_facts` raises `RuntimeError` for a half-populated state row
findings.description: This fails explicitly rather than falling back, which is consistent with the project rules. The cost is that a corrupt `sync_state` row turns every trades request into a 500. That seems acceptable, and it is worth noting that the same guard already exists in `read_trade_status`. The two copies could share a helper to avoid duplication.

findings.title: `_window`/`_count` build SQL through `sql.SQL(table)` with a suppressed lint
findings.description: The table argument is a module-local literal, so this is not injectable today. Using `sql.Identifier` with a schema and table pair, such as `sql.Identifier("kalshi", "trades")`, would remove the need for the `noqa: S608` and make the safety structural.

findings.title: Window resolution and day-boundary extraction
findings.description: Moving `window_start_utc` and `window_end_utc` into one shared module keeps the inclusive-end convention in a single place. `resolve_window` is well documented, and unit tests cover bare dates, naive datetimes, omitted bounds and reversed ranges. The connection is released before the 422 refusal, and a test asserts it. The count-then-fetch ordering with no `LIMIT` is well reasoned, and the integration tests cover inclusive bounds and `count == len(fetch)`.
